## Snyk

Snyk's official CLI MCP server scans application dependencies, source code, infrastructure definitions, SBOMs, and secrets. Use it to investigate vulnerabilities while changing a project and retrieve findings in your assistant.

### Setup

Create a Snyk account, ensure the required scanning products are enabled for your organization, and supply a [Snyk API token](https://docs.snyk.io/snyk-api/authentication-for-api) as `SNYK_TOKEN`. Token authentication requires no OAuth application or custom HTTP headers. Set `SNYK_CFG_ORG` to select an organization and `SNYK_API` when your account uses a regional API endpoint. Mount the project with ToolHive's `--volume <HOST_PROJECT>:/project` option and pass `/project` to the scan tools; complete the server's folder-trust step for directories you intend to scan.

The pinned official Alpine image is Linux amd64 only; ARM hosts need working amd64 container emulation. It supplies a minimal scanner environment, so projects that require additional ecosystem build tools need an appropriate Snyk language image or a separately prepared environment. Dependency scans may invoke project build tools and contact package registries, so this entry allows outbound HTTP and HTTPS. Container scanning can require additional container-runtime access, which this entry does not configure. Follow the [Snyk MCP setup guide](https://docs.snyk.io/agent-security/agentic-security-with-snyk-studio/getting-started-with-snyk-studio) for product access, regional endpoints, and scan requirements.
